item.title: Information: Too Important to Centralize
item.description: Modern warfare runs on information—but centralizing it under a single commander risks slowing decisions and hindering the force. It must be dispersed, empowering leaders at all echelons to act independently and outpace the adversary.

item.title: How to Win the Information Game in Venezuela
item.description: As U.S. strategic interest in Venezuela grows, agentic AI and tailored messaging emerge as critical tools in the information domain—offering influence without escalation.

item.title: Finding Congress
item.description: This week, Bill Reinsch examines Congress’s role in shaping trade policy and proposes ways for lawmakers to delegate its constitutional powers.

item.title: How Important Is Blue Origin’s Second New Glenn Launch?
item.description: With the second launch of New Glenn, Blue Origin becomes only the second space operator in the world to conduct a vertical landing of an orbital-class booster. The Pentagon, NASA, and commercial customers are now counting on Blue Origin to deliver New Glenn at scale.

item.title: Jungle Thunder: A Multinational Approach to Improving U.S. Capabilities in Jungle Warfare
item.description: Senior Associate Wilder Alejandro Sánchez and Andre Carvalho assess the U.S. jungle warfare readiness and propose new mechanisms for cooperation between U.S. and Latin American forces to increase combat readiness.

item.title: Russia’s Intense Air Campaign in October
item.description: Russia's recent missile strikes indicate a transition in strategy and doctrine, where industrial capacity plays a growing role in determining battlefield dynamics. Massed salvos have given way to a more flexible strike schedule, necessitating an adaptive defensive strategy.

item.title: USAID Youth Engagement: A Potential Generation Lost?
item.description: The halting of USAID’s youth programming represents a critical inflection point for U.S. development policy. The termination risks reversing gains in employment, social cohesion, and civic participation that underpin economic and democratic resilience.

item.title: A Complex Legacy: U.S. Global Food Security Assistance, 2008–Present
item.description: Among U.S. global development programs paused or terminated in 2025 are those that aimed to improve global agriculture and nutrition. Through an interactive graphic, CSIS explores the history and status of U.S. government funding for eight of these programs.
